I am 68 years old, and I have been farming the land in Quzhou County since I was a young girl. I never went to school, but I know this land well—its soil, its water, and its seasons. My family has about 4 mu of good flat land on the North China Plain. I do not have the strength to try new fancy crops or take big risks. I know what works here, and so do my neighbors: the winter wheat–summer maize rotation. It feeds my family, and I can sell the surplus.

This year, I will plant winter wheat on all 4 mu in late October, right after the National Day. I will use the improved wheat seed that the seed station sells—it is reliable and gives better grain than the old traditional varieties, and it is not as expensive or tricky as the new hybrids. Before sowing, I will hire the rotary tiller to turn the soil once because the stubble from last year’s maize is still there. For fertilizer, I will put down about 18 jin of nitrogen fertilizer, 7 jin of phosphorus, and 4 jin of potassium per mu, which is what the county extension man recommended last year and what I have always done. I will irrigate three times: once before winter to protect the seedlings from freezing, once at jointing in spring when the wheat is shooting up, and once during grain filling in May. I will spray pesticide twice—once in spring for aphids and once before harvest for diseases if the weather is damp. I expect to harvest around 500 kg per mu in early June.

As soon as the wheat comes off, I will plant summer maize on the same 4 mu. There is no time to waste—the heat and rainfall of summer are short. I will plant hybrid maize seed; everyone uses hybrid maize here because the yield is much higher and the stalks are strong. To save time and labor, I will plant it with no-tillage right into the wheat stubble. I will apply about 16 jin of nitrogen, 5 jin of phosphorus, and 4 jin of potassium per mu. The maize will need two irrigations—one at the big喇叭口 stage and one during grain filling in late August. I will spray pesticide once or twice if the corn borer shows up. If the weather is kind, I expect about 550 kg per mu by late September.

I do not grow vegetables on a large scale because they need too much daily care and market prices go up and down. Wheat and maize are safe. I know how to grow them, and I can manage the work even at my age with some help from my family.
